results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 36 outline summaries of aligned units (p01-p36, with p35 covering the checklist lead-in and list) match the controlling idea of the spec paragraph they are aligned to, in spec order; the three callouts match no paragraph by design.

The five units marked two_ideas hold one idea each against the spec: Introduction ¶2 is thesis plus roadmap by design (p02); Stream-Aligned ¶1 (four types, first one defined) and ¶4 (three serving types under one two-question test, with figure) each equal one controlling idea (p05, p08); Worked Example ¶5 is one inference (twelve teams classify, so the queue was not a fault of type, p29); Checklist ¶2 is the hand-off paragraph carrying the declared callback (p36).

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: scene and pattern to S6, stream-aligned to S1, the three type sections to S2-S4, anti-patterns to S5, the source comparison to S1 and S5, the worked example to S2-S6, the AI section to S3 and S6; no orphan paragraph.

Each quotation, table and figure is introduced or followed by a sentence saying what it shows (the two closing tables by their lead-in sentences, both figures by captions, the decision table by four paragraphs of reasoning).

Sources are named with book and concept (Team Topologies: stream, four types, self-service, complicated-subsystem goal, handovers, ratio, conversions; Empowered: experience and platform teams; Build What Matters: six structures, staffing rule; An Elegant Puzzle: centralized groups); rules of thumb are attributed ('My rule of thumb is three teams or more', 'Treat it as the authors' rule of thumb', 'their rule of thumb for staffing'); extensions are marked ('is my extension' twice, 'By my reading', 'that reading is mine', 'which are mine and not Larson's') and collected under 'The author's synthesis'.

All 31 transition_in boundaries (9 section openings after the first, the paragraph transitions, the conclusion and its four paragraphs) express the declared relationship and pick up the declared carried-over information; the two weakest are still acceptable: Build What Matters ¶ opens on the difference the spec's 'introduces' itself names ('starts from structures and not from types'), and What AI Changes ¶2 opens with 'also' and gives the if-then (cause-effect) in its next sentence.

The hand-off expresses sequence to interaction-modes-and-team-apis, carrying over 'four team types and what each is for' and introducing how teams of those types work with one another and how that agreement is written down.

results.finding: Flow reader A item 2 (a) and flow reader B item 1 (a): neither could work out what 'a fourth, a fifth and a sixth' counts. Corvane has twelve teams (eleven product teams and one platform team), so three more are the 13th-15th overall or the 2nd-4th outside the streams; both readers had to assume it means 'three more teams'. results.draft_locus: Where the Sources Differ: Two Types, Four Types, Six Structures ¶1
results.quote: Readers from product management know the same teams under other names, and the procedure in the next section has to work with those names too.
results.finding: Both flow readers name this section in their answers on placement and reordering (A: 'the one section that felt like a step sideways', 'the only place the momentum dropped'; B: 'the placement before the procedure is only partly clear', 'reads as a detour'), and both propose moving it after the worked example because the procedure and the worked example never use the other books' names. Neither listed it as a lost-thread point rated (a), and A calls the current order followable, so it carries no corroborated_by. The difficulty comes from the order of sections, which the spec's flow and decision log fix deliberately.

Every term on does_not_know is given at or before first use (stream and stream-aligned team, platform team, self-service, enabling team, complicated-subsystem team, functional team, component team in its table row, experience team); cognitive load is glossed; 'count of crossing changes', the 2021 schedules episode and 'fifth stage' (flow reader B items 10, 4, 21) are references to earlier chapters or the book introduction, carry a cross-link, and the crossing condition is restated in full in the same sentence.
The introduction opens on a specific scene with names and numbers, states the stake and bridges to the reader's own experience; the intro reader found none of the weak patterns.

The conclusion does not open with 'in conclusion', adds no new subtopic, holds no body evidence and does not end on a rephrased thesis alone; it sorts what holds by how settled it is, then gives a course of action and the hand-off.

The conclusion states what no single section states (the types as one question asked four ways; a team's name does not answer it; the platform team was of the right type all along and the QA request hid a need an enabling team could meet) and the so-what (list your teams, type each, test every team that is not stream-aligned; put the next request through the four steps). The unstated 'one question' is recorded under flow_is_followable.
The closing paragraph returns to the three requests that reached Dario Vance in one month: none approved as proposed, and the reader is told why each got its answer.

The intro reader predicted all ten sections in the draft's exact order, the kind of evidence (the fictional Corvane case decided at the end, reasoning from hand-offs and load, per-type conditions, a mapping of two product-management books) and the plain, prescriptive tone.

The cold reader classified all four as expected: (1) stream-aligned, (2) none of the four, a functional team that adds a hand-off and one shared queue, (3) enabling, (4) complicated-subsystem, each with the reason and the passages relied on.

Each of the three non-stream types has an explicit do-not-create statement of three cases (platform: one or two teams, no team asked, only by request; enabling: would do the work, a single team's gap, no end date; complicated-subsystem: only unfamiliar code, knowledge learned on the job, most changes need both teams), repeated in the 'Do not create it when' column.

Each pattern names its user and an outcome measure: platform (stream-aligned teams; share of uses without a request, lead time), enabling (the team helped; working alone a quarter after the exit, engagements ended), complicated-subsystem (stream-aligned teams using the part; share of changes needing the team and their wait), and the procedure (the leader who approves teams; share of non-stream teams that can name whom they serve and their measure, the ratio).
